tasks.summary: t4 adds a read-only `codeReview.task.progress` IPC route (handler-runtime.ts:608, task-review-rpc.ts readTaskReviewProgress) backed by `TaskReviewCoordinator.progress()` (coordinator.ts), a typed progress view (progress-view.ts) and a client poller (progress-client.ts) with 5s deterministic polling, 45s-or-change update cadence, and abort-only cancellation that closes just the observation socket. I independently traced every scoped segment at the pinned final commit 31f711098 (current checkout has zero diff from it for all 7 source files; only docs/task-review-execution.md has since gained two unrelated sections from later, out-of-scope commits about review policy/attribution, which do not touch t4's subject matter). `progress()` contains only `loadCheckpoint` reads plus in-memory `active`/`controllers` map lookups — no `save`, no provider resolution, no admission/resume path — confirming AC1. `formatReviewProgress`/`pollTaskReviewProgress` never compute a percentage and explicitly surface `freshness` ('live'/'stale'/'unknown') and, via the two in-scope t5-commit corrections, 'execution inactive; explicit recovery required' when `executionState==='inactive'` and publication isn't complete — confirming AC2. The poller takes an `onUpdate` callback, and `readReviewProgress` destroys only the RPC observation socket on abort (verified against a real `net.Server`/`net.Socket` in the fourth test) without touching review execution — confirming AC3. The stale-controller-leak correction (`owned&&active?.attempt.header.reviewer==='controller'`) is a genuine fix: without it, `progress()` could attribute a daemon-reviewed attempt's status to a stale `this.controllers` entry left from an earlier controller-reviewed attempt on the same path.

testCoverage.explanation: Independently ran `npx tsx --test-force-exit --test src/workflow/code-review/task-review/__tests__/progress-client.test.ts` against the current checkout (zero diff from the pinned commit 31f7110989c95dd55818b9f940b1716ec68549c2 for all 7 scoped files). All 4 named cases passed, each asserting a distinct acceptance behavior: (1) `progress()`/`readTaskReviewProgress` validate repo/reviewId/attempt, reject a path-traversal reviewId (`../escape`, blocked by `checkpointPath`'s `^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_-]{0,127}$` regex), reject a bad attempt, and never invoke the injected provider (`calls===0`); (2) the poller emits at t=0/45000/50000(phase change)/60000(terminal), never includes '%', and the stale-freshness format path reports 'current process activity unknown'/'last meaningful activity unknown'; it also verifies immediate-abort, abort-raced-with-a-late-update (0 updates emitted), and identity-mismatch rejection; (3) a disk-full write failure during the first task leaves the on-disk checkpoint at status='running' with 0 completed tasks (confirmed by tracing `commitResult`'s rollback-on-save-failure path in coordinator.ts, which restores `activeTaskId` and rethrows `persistenceError` before any failure is durably committed), and both the original and a fresh coordinator instance report `executionState:'inactive'` + the 'explicit recovery required' message, stopping after exactly 1 read/0 sleeps with no provider call and no checkpoint mutation; (4) cancellation against a real `net.createServer`/`net.createConnection` pair confirms the RPC socket is destroyed before its 15s deadline and 0 updates are emitted. `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` also passed with zero errors. I additionally located (not part of t4's own change/test scope, but directly relevant corroborating evidence for the one-line coordinator.ts stale-controller-leak correction that IS in t4's scope) a sibling test 'A new daemon attempt never exposes retired controller progress' in progress-e2e.test.ts (added by the adjacent t5 commit a8ba108b, same file set) that exercises exactly that scenario (controller attempt 1 retires, daemon attempt 2 on the same reviewId must not leak attempt 1's controller progress). I was not able to execute that file in this sandbox (command required approval I did not escalate), so I rely on static trace of the fix plus the passing named-test suite for the formal verdict.
